BiblicalUsage: The chapiter is the carved crown on top of a pillar, and nearly every appearance of this word belongs to Solomon's temple. In 1 Kings 7:16 the two chapiters of the great pillars were five cubits high, worked in brass with nets, chains, and rows of pomegranates, and 2 Chronicles 4:12 describes the same work from the other account.
TheologicalSignificance: I am convinced the temple's beauty was not decoration for its own sake; it was craftsmanship offered to God, and I believe the care poured into those capitals still says something true about worship that costs us our best work.
